Hit two real bugs while scripting this, both fixed before the final build: (1) figma's layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical='FILL' throws unless the node already has an auto-layout parent -- fixed by only setting FILL after appendChild, never before; left two rounds of debris (an empty container, then a stray unparented card instance + loose frames) on the page from the failed attempts, cleaned up via node.remove() before the next try. (2) figma.createFrame() defaults to a fixed 100x100 that does NOT auto-hug content just because layoutMode is set -- every custom auto-layout frame (legend row/items, titleGroup, filters row, header, container) needed primaryAxisSizingMode/counterAxisSizingMode explicitly set to 'AUTO'; missed this on the first successful-looking run and the header silently inflated to 216px tall, squeezing the chart body to 1px (still 'succeeded', only caught via a read-back verify + PNG export, not by the script returning cleanly) -- worth remembering for any future Figma-scripted auto-layout frame.
Verified via read-back (positions/sizes match the ported math exactly: small body 388x142, large body 788x344, bars capped at 24px thick in both) and a PNG export of the whole container, visually near-identical to the live browser screenshots. One faithful-to-code finding surfaced by the export, flagged to the user rather than fixed unilaterally: on the small card the y-axis has only ~58px of plot height for 6 ticks (0/5/10/15/20/25), so the tick labels visually crowd -- a real spacing tradeoff in the component's current PADDING, not a Figma-mock artifact.

Added 4 new semantic tokens: color/text/{brand,success,warning,danger}-solid, each an alias of the matching color/background/<tone> token (brand.600/green.600/amber.500/red.600) rather than a hand-picked shade -- so a legend label or similar text that needs to visually match a solid bar/fill can never drift from that fill's actual color if the shade is ever re-tuned again (directly motivated by noticing the chart colors drifted 500->400 in Figma without a code update -- see below).
Motivated by a real accessibility finding, not just naming tidiness: computed contrast by hand for the existing tone-700 text tokens against their own badge's subtle-100 background -- text.success (green.700) sits at ~4.56:1 on green.100 (barely passes AA), but green.600 on the same background drops to ~3.00:1 (fails). text.danger (red.700) is 5.30:1, red.600 drops to 3.95:1 (also fails, even accounting for Badge's semibold label weight, which doesn't clear WCAG's large-text exception at 12-16px). Confirmed migrating the existing 700 tokens down to 600 to match solid fills would have broken contrast on every existing Badge/pill -- these are additive-only, the original text.<tone> (700) tokens are untouched.
text/warning-solid deliberately aliases color/background/warning (amber.500), NOT color/background/warning-strong (orange) -- confirmed with the user that the orange warning-strong hue is scoped exclusively to the alert-pill system, not a general 'attention' tone.

Fix: build-02/03's apply loop now reads each variable's current value before writing. New variable -> create + write (unchanged). Worth remembering: build:tokens alone is NOT sufficient after a token change if anything needs to render live in this repo's own preview harness -- always run the full `npm run build` (or at least scripts/bundle-styles.mjs) too, not just the tokens step, or CSS var lookups will silently resolve to nothing with no error.
